payload.name: argv-duplicates
payload.pins: repeated arguments are retained, in place.

payload.name: base-present
payload.pins: `base`, when present, is the **last** key of `[certificate.vcs]`, after `untracked`, and is covered by the signature like everything else.

payload.name: content-manifest
payload.pins: `content` is emitted **verbatim**, whatever its algorithm — here `manifest-v1-sha256`, the non-git one — and `base` is absent.

payload.name: crlf-multiline
payload.pins: A physical newline inside a multi-line basic or literal string is LF regardless of the document's line endings; escaped CR and CRLF values are preserved (Canonical-Payload.md §5, §4).

payload.name: escapes
payload.pins: every escape in the table, only those escapes, and the fact that sorting happens **before** escaping.

payload.name: minimal
payload.pins: the baseline shape — required fields only, every optional key absent rather than empty.

payload.name: multiple-commands
payload.pins: command entries stay in execution order, each preceded by exactly one blank line.

payload.name: non-ascii-literal
payload.pins: UTF-8 is emitted literally, and no Unicode normalization is applied.

payload.name: scoped
payload.pins: `paths` is present, sorted, deduplicated, and sits between `repo` and `content`.

payload.name: signed
payload.pins: `key_id` is present and last in `[certificate]`, after `issuer`.

payload.name: targets-duplicates
payload.pins: duplicate target names are removed before sorting, while the same repetition survives verbatim inside `argv`.

payload.name: targets-single
payload.pins: the one-element array has no separator and no trailing comma.

payload.name: targets-unicode
payload.pins: sorting is over UTF-8 **bytes** — not locale collation, and not UTF-16 code units.

payload.name: targets-unsorted-input
payload.pins: `targets` is sorted on output even though the input is in run order — and `argv` is *not*, in the same vector.

payload.name: unscoped
payload.pins: an empty scope is a whole-repository claim, and is omitted from the payload entirely.

payload.name: untracked-true
payload.pins: `untracked = true` is emitted as a bare TOML boolean, and moves independently of `content`.

signature.name: escapes
signature.pins: a signature over a payload containing every escape in the table, including the sort-before-escape ordering trap.

signature.name: minimal
signature.pins: the happy path — the canonical payload of `vectors/payload/minimal`, signed under the namespace the standard names, and verifying against the registered public key.

signature.name: mutated-payload
signature.pins: the signature covers the payload bytes, and one flipped bit is enough. **This vector MUST fail.**

signature.name: unicode
signature.pins: a signature over a payload full of multi-byte UTF-8, so an implementation that re-encodes or escapes non-ASCII fails at the signature rather than silently producing a different claim.

signature.name: wrong-key
signature.pins: the signature must verify **against the registered key**, not merely be a valid signature. **This vector MUST fail.**

signature.name: wrong-namespace
signature.pins: domain separation is applied, not ignored. **This vector MUST fail.**

content.name: byte-order
content.pins: `manifest-v1` sorts by the raw bytes of the **full path**, so `a.b` precedes `a/b`, which precedes `a0`.

content.name: empty-scope
content.pins: a scope matching no tracked entry has a well-defined id — the empty tree, or the digest of no records — and `src/d` matches nothing although it is a string prefix of `src/db`.

content.name: modes
content.pins: all four entry kinds — regular file, executable file, symbolic link, nested repository — and what each contributes.

content.name: non-ascii-path
content.pins: a path is the byte sequence the VCS records — no Unicode normalisation, no case folding — so two names that render identically are two different files.

content.name: order-independent
content.pins: the entries arrive in no particular order, and the ids do not depend on it.

content.name: scope-keeps-paths
content.pins: a scoped `git-tree` id keeps **full repository paths** — it is not the id of the subtree at the scoped directory — and the scope `src/db` does not take in `src/dbx`.

content.name: sha256-object-format
content.pins: `git-tree-sha256` — the same entries as `order-independent`, under git's SHA-256 object format.

verify.name: content-differs
verify.pins: the content comparison is an equality test, failing it is an ordinary not-covered — and a `base` equal to the commit under evaluation does not rescue it.

verify.name: content-malformed
verify.pins: a malformed content id is **decidably invalid** — rejected, never repaired, and never unverifiable.

verify.name: content-matches-other-base
verify.pins: a certificate is matched by **content**, never by commit — one whose `base` is not the commit under evaluation, but whose `content` matches, covers it.

verify.name: content-unknown-algorithm
verify.pins: an algorithm the consumer cannot compute is **not a mismatch** — the record is unevaluated and the outcome is unverifiable.

verify.name: coverage-union
verify.pins: required coverage is the **union** of several certificates, not a property any single one has to satisfy.

verify.name: earlier-draft-record
verify.pins: a record in the pre-2026-10-09 shape — `commit`, `clean`, no `content` — is **decidably invalid**: not covered, never unverifiable, and never translated.

verify.name: empty-key-store
verify.pins: an empty key store means "no signers are trusted", never "no restrictions".

verify.name: other-framework
verify.pins: an unrecognised `framework` is **ignored** — neither counted as evidence nor treated as an error.

verify.name: revoked-key
verify.pins: revocation beats cryptography, and it is a status flip rather than a deletion.

verify.name: scope-too-narrow
verify.pins: a scoped certificate is not a whole-repository certificate.

verify.name: unknown-keys
verify.pins: unknown keys or tables make a v1 record malformed at every level, including the root and the excluded signature block.

verify.name: unknown-schema
verify.pins: an unimplemented schema version is unverifiable, not not-covered.

verify.name: unknown-schema-off-platform
verify.pins: a record the consumer cannot interpret is **potentially relevant whatever its fields appear to say**, so the outcome is `unverifiable` even though the record looks irrelevant.

verify.name: unreadable-store
verify.pins: the third outcome. *We could not tell* is a different answer from *we could tell, and it is not covered*.

verify.name: unreadable-store-off-platform
verify.pins: a record the consumer **can** interpret but could not verify makes the outcome `unverifiable` **only if its interpreted scope could satisfy some part of the requirement**. This one cannot, so the outcome is `not-covered`.

verify.name: unsigned-required
verify.pins: a consumer that requires signatures rejects unsigned certificates outright — and both spellings of "unsigned" mean the same thing.

verify.name: unverifiable-but-covered
verify.pins: precedence — unverifiable wins over not-covered, but not over a requirement already met.

verify.name: wrong-platform
verify.pins: certificates for another platform contribute nothing.

store.name: manifest-content
store.pins: a `manifest-v1-sha256` content id is split like any other, giving a `manifest-v1-sha256` directory and a 64-digit digest directory.

store.name: scoped
store.pins: a scoped certificate is stored under its own, **scoped** content id: the directory is the certificate's `content`, never the whole-repository id of the same tree.

store.name: signed
store.pins: a signed certificate is named by the hash of its canonical payload, which includes `key_id` and excludes the signature block — so it is stored next to, not on top of, its unsigned twin.

store.name: signed-non-canonical
store.pins: the name is the hash of the canonical payload reconstructed from the parsed fields, never of the file bytes — a non-canonical rendering of `store/signed`, signature block included, is stored under `store/signed`'s name.

store.name: signed-non-canonical-no-block
store.pins: removing a signed certificate's signature block does not change its name — `key_id` is part of the payload and stays, the block never was — so the stripped copy and the signed one land on the same name.

store.name: unsigned
store.pins: an unsigned certificate is stored at `v1/<algorithm>/<digest>/<payload-hash>.toml`, with the content id split at its first `:` and the name the SHA-256 of the canonical payload.

store.name: unsigned-empty-block
store.pins: the empty-signature-block form of an unsigned certificate is stored under the same name as the form with no block at all.

notes.name: appended
notes.pins: a writer adds a record whose payload is not yet present after the last piece, behind its own delimiter, leaving every existing byte unchanged.

notes.name: corrupt-middle
notes.pins: a piece that does not parse is reported and skipped, and the records on either side of it are still yielded.

notes.name: duplicate-not-added
notes.pins: a writer does not add a record whose payload is already present — publishing the same certificate twice changes nothing.

notes.name: escaped-newline
notes.pins: the delimiter cannot occur inside a canonical record, even when a value contains a newline followed by the delimiter's exact text — the newline is written as the two characters `\n`, so the text never starts a line.

notes.name: foreign-preamble
notes.pins: text before the first delimiter is reported and skipped, never parsed as a record — even when, as here, it would parse.

notes.name: signed-and-unsigned
notes.pins: two records with different payloads share a note: a signed one, whose signature table follows its payload after one blank line, and an unsigned one.

notes.name: signed-replaces-unsigned
notes.pins: a signed record whose payload is already present, unsigned, replaces the present record in place.

notes.name: single-unsigned
notes.pins: the framing of a one-record note — a delimiter line, then the record, and nothing after it.

notes.name: unsigned-copy-not-added
notes.pins: an unsigned copy of a present signed record is the same payload, so it is not added, and it never replaces the signed one.
